en: Mayon Volcano has a six-kilometer Permanent Danger Zone to protect people from sudden explosions and lava flows.
Coastal provinces like Surigao del Sur must have clear evacuation routes because the Pacific Ocean can generate dangerous tsunamis after earthquakes.
PAGASA monitors the heat index to warn students when high humidity and temperature cause dangerous heat exhaustion during outdoor recess.
Avoid swimming in the polluted Pasig River to prevent leptospirosis, a severe bacterial infection transmitted through water contaminated by rat urine.
When PAGASA raises Signal Number Two, strong winds can uproot trees, so children should stay indoors away from glass windows.
Clearing stagnant rainwater in old tires prevents Aedes aegypti mosquitoes from breeding and spreading the deadly dengue virus in your neighborhood.
Hikers climbing Mount Pulag must wear thick jackets because the high altitude causes temperatures to drop below freezing, risking dangerous hypothermia.
Applying sunscreen is crucial in the Philippines because its location near the equator exposes children to intense ultraviolet rays that cause sunburns.
Residents in mountainous Benguet province must plant deep-rooted trees on slopes to prevent soil erosion and protect homes from deadly landslides.
Wearing water shoes while snorkeling in Tubbataha Reef protects children from stepping on sharp corals and getting painful cuts from sea urchins.
Wearing an N95 mask during heavy traffic in Metro Manila filters out dangerous particulate matter to protect children's developing lungs from asthma.
Never drink untreated water from Laguna de Bay because agricultural runoff introduces harmful bacteria that cause severe stomach illnesses and diarrhea.
